title: The 5 Biggest Objects in the Asteroid Belt, Ranked (#1 Isn't an Asteroid)

scenes.text: The five biggest objects in the asteroid belt, ranked. Number one isn't officially an asteroid anymore.

scenes.label: Interamnia · ~330 km
scenes.text: Number five: Interamnia. About three hundred thirty kilometers across, around two hundred miles of rock.

scenes.label: Hygiea · ~430 km
scenes.text: Number four: Hygiea. About four hundred thirty kilometers wide, and scientists still debate if it deserves a dwarf planet label.

scenes.label: Pallas · ~512 km
scenes.text: Number three: Pallas. About five hundred twelve kilometers across, almost a perfect tie with number two.

scenes.label: Vesta · ~525 km
scenes.text: Number two: Vesta. About five hundred twenty-five kilometers across, barely wider than Pallas.

scenes.label: Ceres · ~940 km
scenes.text: Number one: Ceres. About nine hundred forty kilometers across, a dwarf planet holding over a third of the whole belt's mass.

description:
The five biggest objects in the asteroid belt, ranked by diameter.
Number one was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006 and holds over a third of the belt's mass.
Which of these would you want to visit?
first_comment: Did you know Ceres is a dwarf planet? What space ranking should we do next?
